```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab11", title = "Fourier seasonality")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "For quarterly data, seasonal dummies use how many extra coefficients (one quarter omitted)?",
  q2 = "Fourier K=1 for a quarterly series uses how many sine/cosine coefficients?",
  q3 = "K = m/2 is special because it is:",
  q4 = "For Beer, would you stop at K=1 or go to K=2? One sentence."
)
```

## What you will do

Compare dummy seasonality with a few Fourier harmonics.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("3", correct = TRUE),
  answer("4"),
  answer("1"),
  answer("12"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("2", correct = TRUE),
  answer("1"),
  answer("4"),
  answer("8"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("The Nyquist frequency (one coefficient, not a pair)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The same as a random walk"),
  answer("Always worse than K=1"),
  answer("Only used for annual data"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Look at residual seasonality and AICc within the regression family.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
